# `@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-editor`

> Token-themed Monaco editor: CodeEditor, DiffEditor, CodeWorkspace.

Part of **brand-ui**, a source-owned, token-driven React component system.
These packages are **private** and published to GitHub Packages.

## Install

You need a token — GitHub Packages has no anonymous read for private packages.
Add to your project's `.npmrc`:

```ini
@qlik-coe-emea:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN}
```

`GITHUB_TOKEN` must be a **classic** PAT with the `read:packages` scope —
fine-grained PATs do not reliably work with this registry. Then:

```bash
pnpm add @qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-editor
```

## Set up styling (do not skip)

Components are Tailwind v4 classes backed by semantic tokens. Two lines in
your CSS entry, or **everything renders unstyled** — the single most common
mistake:

```css
@import "@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-tokens/styles.css";
@source "../node_modules/@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-editor/dist";
```

The `@source` line is required because Tailwind ignores `node_modules`. Add
one per brand-ui package you render. Then wrap your app once:

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-tokens";

<ThemeProvider defaultTheme="qlik-bright">{children}</ThemeProvider>;
```

## This package specifically

- `monaco-editor` is a peer — it owns `globalThis.MonacoEnvironment`, so two copies break it.
- Import `.../monaco-environment` once at your app entry to enable language workers (Vite-only).
- `./markdown/parse` and `./markdown/frontmatter` are pure, Monaco-free and server-safe.

## What's in it

8 exported components — including `CodeEditor`, `CodeWorkspace`, `CopyButton`, `DiffEditor`, `EDITOR_LANGUAGES`.

Don't guess the API — ask the CLI:

```bash
pnpm add -D @qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-cli
pnpm exec brand-ui search <query>   # find a component
pnpm exec brand-ui docs <Name>      # its real props, from source
```

## Using an AI coding agent?

Install the CLI above and, for Claude Code, the plugin:

```
/plugin marketplace add Qlik-CoE-EMEA/qlabs-components
/plugin install brand-ui
```

`brand-ui docs <Name>` returns intent, composition, state→token mappings and
anti-patterns — tell your agent to run it instead of guessing a prop. The CLI
also runs as an MCP server (`brand-ui mcp`).

## Package detail

A token-themed [Monaco Editor](https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor) (the
editor that powers VS Code) wrapped as brand-ui components.

## What this is (and isn't)

Monaco is a **monolithic, self-rendering editor engine** — it mounts into one DOM
node and draws all of its own widgets (autocomplete, find/replace, context menu,
hovers, minimap). Those widgets **cannot** be swapped for brand-ui React
components without forking VS Code. So this package does the two things that
actually make Monaco "fit" the design system:

1. **Themes the inside** via Monaco's theming API — the editor surface _and_ its
   widgets are recolored from the active `data-theme` across all six brand themes
   (the oklch→hex bridge in `lib/monaco-theme-bridge.ts`).
2. **Wraps it in brand-ui chrome** — `EditorToolbar`, `CodeWorkspace` tabs and the
   copy button are brand-ui (`Button`, `Select`, `Tabs`).

This mirrors how `@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-flow` wraps React Flow and `@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-data` wraps TanStack:
a powerful third-party engine behind a token-driven brand API. It is intentionally
**not** "source-owned" the way primitives in `@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-ui` are.

## Components

| Component       | Purpose                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CodeEditor`    | Single editable Monaco editor (controlled/uncontrolled) |
| `DiffEditor`    | Side-by-side / inline diff (original ↔ modified)        |
| `CodeWorkspace` | Multi-file shell — brand-ui `Tabs` over one editor      |
| `EditorToolbar` | Filename + language `Select` + copy `Button` chrome     |

For **read-only** syntax-highlighted display (not editing), use `CodeBlock` from
`@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-ai` (Shiki) instead.

## Workers (required for IntelliSense)

Monaco runs language services in web workers. Import the worker setup **once** at
your app entry (Vite):

```ts
import "@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-editor/monaco-environment";
```

Without it the editor still renders and highlights, but completions/diagnostics
are unavailable. `?worker` is a Vite-only transform — non-Vite bundlers must set
`self.MonacoEnvironment.getWorker(Url)` themselves.

## Usage

```tsx
import { CodeEditor } from "@qlik-coe-emea/qlabs-components-editor";

<div className="h-[420px]">
  <CodeEditor language="typescript" defaultValue="const a = 1;" onChange={setValue} />
</div>;
```

The editor reads the active theme from `data-theme` (set by `ThemeProvider`) and
re-themes automatically on change — no extra wiring.

## SSR

Components are `"use client"`. `monaco-editor` references browser globals at import
time, so in RSC/SSR apps load the editor in a client-only boundary (e.g. a dynamic
import with SSR disabled).
